name: 王可
objective:
本課程將閱讀並討論聯合國 2030 年持續發展議程的議題，主題和做法。 藉由對全球繁榮，社會平等和環境可持續性共同藍圖的認識，學生能進一步參加全球活動，並在本地和跨域發展共同夥伴關係，以參與持續發展目標的行動。 此外，學生將能夠通過批判性閱讀和討論來強化英語能力，並為與可持續發展目標有關的更深入的交流做好準備。
This course will read and discuss issues, topics, and practices of the UN’s 2030 agenda for sustainable development, adopted by all UN member states. With full insights and comprehensive views of the shared blueprint for global prosperity, social equality and environmental sustainability, students are expected to participate in global activities and form partnership locally and across borders to engage in SDGs actions. In addition, students will be able to enhance their English competence through critical reading and discussion, and will be prepared for more in-depth communication pertaining to the SDGs.
schedule:
1　Course Introduction; SDGs Overview; Discussion Norms; AI Expectations
2　Reading Strategies; Explaining Data & Infographics; Taiwan Engineering Cases
3　Facilitation Training; Discussion Skills; Data Description Practice
4　SDG 9 Industry, Innovation & Infrastructure
5　SDG 7 Affordable & Clean Energy
6　SDG 12 Responsible Consumption & Production
7　SDG 11 Sustainable Cities & Communities
8　SDG 13 Climate Action; Portfolio Check
9　Midterm Skills Consolidation
10　Project Introduction; Taiwan Engineering SDG Case Selection
11　Evaluating Solutions: Feasibility, Constraints, Tradeoffs
12　Evidence & Explanation Workshop; GEPT Practice
13　Project Workshop I (Stakeholders & Evidence)
14　Project Workshop II (Solution Design & Slides)
15　Project Workshop III; Rehearsal
16　Final Presentations (Part I)
17　Final Presentations (Part II)
18　University Exam / Course Wrap-Up
scorePolicy:
University-Wide English Exam: 20%

GEPT Speaking & Writing Test: 10%

Participation & Preparedness: 20%
Active participation in structured discussions, completion of in-class tasks, respectful listening and engagement, and basic preparation for weekly topics.

Class Work Portfolio: 15%
Collection of selected in-class work (checked mid-semester and at the end). May include short reflections, vocabulary notes, data description tasks, stakeholder maps, and discussion worksheets. Graded for completion and engagement.

Student-Led Facilitation: 10%
In groups, students lead one SDG-themed class segment using a guided facilitation format. Assessed on clarity of explanation, vocabulary support, Taiwan connection, and ability to guide discussion and Q&A.

Final Project & Presentation: 25%
Group presentation plus Q&A on a Taiwan-linked engineering SDG case, including problem overview, stakeholders and tradeoffs, feasibility considerations, and a proposed response.
